chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from al-Jahm ibn al-Hakam from Isma'il ibn Muslim said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Asceticism (zuhd) in the world is not the squandering of wealth, nor the prohibiting of the permissible, but rather asceticism in it is that you do not consider what is in your hand more secure/trustworthy than what is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.الزُّهْدُ: Asceticism or renunciation of the world

ai.seo_question: What is the true definition of asceticism (zuhd) in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that true asceticism (zuhd) is not the destruction of wealth or forbidding what is lawful, but a state of mind where one does not rely more on their current possessions than on God's promise. This teaching emphasizes spiritual trust in God over material security, aligning with the Shia scholarly tradition that views zuhd as a quality of the heart rather than mere poverty. It encourages believers to maintain their worldly duties while keeping their ultimate reliance fixed on divine providence.
